title: Indicators and methods for assessing acoustical preferences and needs of students in educational buildings: A review

findings.consequent: Students' well-being and performance in educational buildings
findings.quote: Sounds (e.g., human activity, nature, building systems) are one of the indoor environmental stimuli that may have positive and/or negative effects on students' well-being and performance in educational buildings.

findings.consequent: Annoyance and adverse health effects in schools
findings.quote: Noise, being one of these stressors, stimulates both the sympathetic nervous system and the endocrine system [7]. Noise was found to be the most annoying factor in schools buildings [6].

findings.consequent: Students' self-rated health, short-term memory, and cognitive performance
findings.quote: On the contrary, positive sounds that have restorative effects (e.g., water fountain) have shown to enhance students' self-rated health as well as improve the students' short-term memory and cognitive performance [20,21].
the effects of indoor acoustics on students' physiological health have been tested by various researchers [33-38].
It was concluded that SCL recovery was fast during the exposure to natural sound.
The results showed that sound pressure level (SPL) had a negative impact on both EDA and RR, while HR was not influenced by the SPL.

findings.consequent: Mental fatigue, heart rate (HR), and working memory of students
findings.quote: The outcomes showed that a high amount of SPL (65-75 dBA) could cause mental fatigue of students, which significantly affected their HR and working memory.
Environmental stressors such as noise play a vital role in affecting an individual's comfort, and it is strongly dependent on the individual's psychological state [40].

findings.antecedent: Lower background noise levels (e.g., airflow through ventilation systems)
findings.consequent: Perception as suitable sound in informal learning spaces
findings.quote: Scannell [13] indicated that some spaces with lower background noise levels (such as airflow through ventilation systems) were perceived by students as suitable sound in informal learning spaces.

findings.consequent: Primary school children's stress, fatigue, and headache
findings.quote: Wålinder et al. [46] proved that noise affected primary school children (fourth grade) negatively by increasing their stress which caused health issues such as fatigue and headache (physiological indicators).
It was concluded that participants had a shorter time response while they were exposed to noise, which was related to a higher stress level based on the arousal theory.

findings.antecedent: Speech noise (with increased Speech Transmission Index - STI)
findings.quote: Acoustical indicators sound types such as speech noise had a significant negative effect on participants' performance and the effects were stronger by increasing the speech transmission index (STI) of the noise [48].
It was found that 38% of students were bothered by noise while they were performing a complex cognitive task (e.g., studying for an exam, reading, and writing).
Tristan-Hernandez et al. [15] observed the negative effect of the background noise generated inside six university facilities on changes in students' attentional processes.
The outcomes showed that there were significant interactions between the effect of the acoustical indicators; sound type and SPL on the children's performance.

findings.consequent: Children's accuracy while performing a perception task
findings.quote: They concluded that a longer RT affected the children's accuracy while performing a perception task.

findings.consequent: Noise annoyance perceived by individuals in an indoor environment
findings.quote: Also, the visual indicators such as greenery elements and water features proved to reduce the noise annoyance perceived by individuals in an indoor environment.
Chung et al. [51] found that the participants (undergraduate students) preferred sea views more than road views, since sea views attenuated the noise annoyance, while road views aggravated it.

findings.antecedent: Combination of low intelligibility background speech and static lighting
findings.quote: It was found that individuals perform better with the combination of low intelligibility background speech and static lighting.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to short-term and long-term thermal strains
findings.quote: Pellerin and Candas [54] mentioned that the perception of indoor acoustics might be affected by exposure to short-term and long-term thermal strains.
In addition, the exposure to high noise levels contributed to thermal discomfort.

findings.antecedent: Sound of primary school children talking
findings.quote: Bluyssen et al. [55] found that listening to the sound of primary school children talking could negatively affect the evaluation of smell.

findings.antecedent: Combined environment (30 °C temperature, odour irritants, VOCs, road traffic noises)
findings.quote: The outcome indicated that individuals' stress levels increased by the exposure to the combined environment of 30 °C temperature, odour irritants volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and road traffic noises.

findings.antecedent: Room temperature, background noise level, and floor impact noise levels
findings.consequent: Loudness and noisiness of floor impact noise
findings.quote: It was found that the loudness and noisiness of the floor impact noise were affected by the room temperature, background noise level, and floor impact noise levels.

findings.antecedent: High noise levels and high air temperature (30 °C)
findings.consequent: Mean value of neurophysiological responses of students
findings.quote: It was proved that high noise levels as well as high air temperature (30 °C) could increase the mean value of neurophysiological responses of students.

findings.consequent: Physiological indicators (blood pressure, HR, skin temperature)
findings.quote: It was revealed that the physiological indicators; blood pressure, HR, and skin temperature were influenced by all the three indicators of the IEQ-factors.

findings.antecedent: Sounds induced by mobile phones, personal music players, and construction sites
findings.quote: The questionnaire's results indicated that sounds induced by mobile phones, personal music players, and construction sites were rated as the most annoying sounds; while footsteps and page-turning sounds were the least annoying.
It was found that the soundscape quality was influenced by the space activity and the acoustical perception.

Based on their expectations, students might be annoyed by speech sounds in the classroom and by fan sounds in computer laboratories. However, speech sound was perceived as the most annoying sound source in both spaces.

findings.consequent: Disturbance and negative effect on concentration in open study spaces
findings.quote: The results showed that the sounds generated by human activities were the most disturbing and negatively affected students' concentration.

findings.consequent: Worse self-rated health and reduced restorative quality
findings.quote: The outcomes of this study indicated that exposure to mechanical sounds resulted in worse self-rated health which reduced restorative quality.
It was shown that positive indoor soundscapes, such as nature sounds (e.g., birdsong and flowing water), have a significant impact in improving self-rated health during social distancing times.

findings.antecedent: Sounds generated by other people (e.g., walking, talking)
findings.consequent: Annoyance for remote workers, loss of concentration, inability to relax
findings.quote: They concluded that 25% of these workers found sounds generated by other people (e.g., walking, talking) as the most annoying sound sources. This annoyance resulted in the loss of concentration and inability to relax.
The study revealed that among all sounds, water and fountain sounds showed the best restorative effects on children's cognitive performance.
Adding to that, exposure to both fountain and stream sounds showed a better performance in short-term memory.
It was indicated that the soundscapes that were perceived as pleasant had positive effects on fatigue restoration and reduced the annoyance level of individuals.

findings.consequent: Individuals' autonomic functions during stressful tasks and resting
findings.quote: This study asserted that soundscapes can influence individuals' autonomic functions during both activities.

According to the results found by Medvedev et al. [85], physiological measurements of the SCL were significantly associated with soundscapes' psychological responses as to pleasantness and eventfulness.

findings.consequent: Students' acoustical preferences and needs, and performance
findings.quote: This outcome showed that improving the acoustical quality, such as reducing the RT, does not always fulfill all students' acoustical preferences and needs, in this case their performance.

findings.antecedent: Natural visual scenes (greenery, water elements, sea view)
findings.consequent: Annoyance perception of the sound source
findings.quote: In addition, natural visual scenes such as greenery, water elements, and sea view play a significant role in reducing the annoyance perception of the sound source.

findings.antecedent: Physical environment elements (e.g., acoustical walls, absorbing ceiling panels)
findings.consequent: Acoustical quality in an indoor environment
findings.quote: In terms of indoor acoustics, physical environment elements, such as the presence of acoustical walls and absorbing ceiling panels, can affect the acoustical quality in an indoor environment [17,49,55].

findings.antecedent: Space layout of an educational building
findings.quote: Additionally, space layout of an educational building can play a vital role in acoustical comfort [69].
